title: Telling parents about school menu changes in Dubai

excerpt: A communication timeline, a message checklist and a worked nursery example for school menu changes.
body_html:
Menu changes are routine in schools and nurseries — a seasonal rotation, a supplier change, a dish retired after low uptake — but telling parents about school menu changes is where most friction starts. Parents plan lunches, manage allergies and answer the same question at home every evening, so a change announced casually reads as a change that can be argued with. This guide gives a simple timeline, a message checklist and a worked example for communicating a change once, clearly. If your school is reviewing its meal provision, start with institutional catering in Dubai.

A timeline that prevents repeat questions

WhenWhat parents receive
Two weeks beforeNotice of the change, the reason and the start date
One week beforeThe new menu itself, in the same format as the old one
Two days beforeA short reminder with the contact for questions
End of the first weekA brief note on uptake and any tweak already made
End of termThe term's changes summarised in one place

What every menu-change message should include

  • What changes, what stays the same, and the exact start date.
  • One plain-language reason — seasonality, a nutrition review, supplier or feedback.
  • How allergens are labelled on the new menu, and where the full list lives.
  • What parents should do if a child has a specific requirement.
  • One named contact channel and the typical reply window.

Handling allergy and dietary questions

Allergy questions deserve their own route, not a comment thread on the menu post. Point parents to the school's established process — usually a form or a direct line to the catering contact — and keep medical decisions with each child's own qualified professional. The message's job is to say clearly where that conversation happens.

A worked message (hypothetical)

A nursery replaces its Thursday hot lunch with a weekly rotating dish from the new term menu. Two weeks out, parents receive three lines: what changes and from when; the reason in one sentence; where the full new menu and the allergy labelling live. One reminder follows two days before. In the first week, two parents ask about the rotation; both are answered through the named contact, and the reception desk fields none of the repeated questions it used to.

Next step: put the communication timeline next to the menu itself when you review institutional catering in Dubai, so changes arrive as a schedule rather than a surprise. Related reading: switching school meal caterers and Dubai school food rules.
